summary: Read-only priority and significance audit, checked against primary sources as of 2026-10-15. MATH: The Thas–Zagier (TZ) bound n<2×10^11 still appears to be the largest published computational exclusion. Every later work I found is structural or restates TZ. Xia's arXiv:1707.05486v7 (EJC 2023) is the latest version and gives characteristic-3 necessary conditions with no new numerical range. Xia's 2018 Math. Comp. paper covers index m≤22 only. The Momihara–Wang–Xiang 2018 survey still reports TZ as the state of the art. None of the 23 OpenAlex citers of TZ, the author pages, or OEIS showed a stronger bound. These are search misses, not proof that none exists. A fully exact replay to 2,582,236,504,064 would be a ×12.9 extension of TZ's own base-two sieve under the same premises. It would not be a new method, and it says nothing about all orders. INFO: The lane's elementary result (balanced maximum NL ∈ {240,242}) is not new relative to the 13 Oct 2026 preprints. The identical two inequalities (488<512 and 253952<2^18) appear in the proof of Proposition 1 of arXiv:2610.17871v1. Proposition 1 alone already shows that no balanced function reaches 244. The support-XOR congruence W≡4ω·b (mod 8) appears in arXiv:2610.17897v1 §3. The step 'balanced and deg≤7 ⇒ 8|W' is the classical Sarkar–Maitra/Carlet divisibility. The parent's new J_h, and its canonical signed spectrum K, are the normalization used in WLW's proof of Theorem 1, applied with m=8. The parent's fixed-half capacity bound is the same device as WLW Lemma 4 (|A|+|B|≤24). Both 2026 preprints still list balanced 9-variable NL 242 as open, and no later claim was located.

findings.claim: TZ baseline: the base-two search on n≡8 (mod 24) up to 2×10^11 found nothing beyond n=2 and n=8. The computation is described in prose only, with no certificate.
findings.quote: Continuing the search up to 2 × 10^11, now with n restricted to the congruence class 8 (mod 24), led to no further solutions (computation time roughly 3 days)
findings.stance: baseline premise imported by the lane
findings.specific_read_scope: entire PDF, including Thm 1.1, Thm 1.3, Prop 2.1, Thm 2.4, §2 summary, Thm 3.1, Thm 4.1/4.2, Conj 4.3, Thm 5.1 and the appendix

findings.claim: TZ census of base-two exceptions: all even n<5×10^9 give exactly 2, 8, 24, 90, 512, 134217728, 297474474. The lane's C runs report the same seven.
findings.quote: we first did this for all (even) n up to 5 × 10^9 (this took about four hours), finding only the following seven solutions in this range

findings.claim: TZ attribute 8|n to Feit. They derive n≡2 (mod 3) from n^3≡1 and n^(n+1)≡1. They credit d^(n+1)≡1 for divisors d of n to Feit, with an elementary proof in K. Thas (2003).
findings.quote: (The divisibility of n by 8 was proved by Feit in the previously cited paper [4], and we must have n ≡ 2 (mod 3) because both n^3 and n^(n+1) are congruent to 1 modulo p.)
findings.specific_read_scope: appendix and the paragraph after Thm 1.3

findings.claim: Base-two necessity is stated by TZ.
findings.quote: a prime p = n^2 + n + 1 can only be special if 2 ∈ D_n, i.e., if 2^(n+1) ≡ 1 (mod p).
findings.stance: the lane's filter is TZ's filter, not a new method

findings.claim: The reduction depends on CFSG through Kantor's theorem.
findings.quote: Kantor’s result, whose proof invokes the classification of finite simple groups, is as follows.

findings.claim: Feit's power-of-two exclusion and Ott's prime-power claim are flagged as erroneous.
findings.quote: Unfortunately, both proofs appear to contain mistakes
findings.stance: supports the lane's exclusion of these results

findings.claim: TZ contain a minor internal inconsistency. The first sentence of the appendix says 2×10^22, while the abstract, §2 and §4 say p<4×10^22, which is consistent with n<2×10^11.
findings.quote: there are no special primes less than 2 × 10^22

findings.claim: Xia's main theorem gives structural necessary conditions: polynomial systems over characteristic 3, with n≡8 (mod 24). It gives no numerical range.
findings.quote: If there exists a finite non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane of order n with v points, then v = n² + n + 1 is prime with n ≡ 8 (mod 24) and n > 8
findings.stance: later structural result; not a stronger bound
findings.specific_read_scope: entire arXiv v7: Thm 1.3, §3, Thm 3.7, §4, §5 conjectures, references

findings.claim: Attribution discrepancy for 8|n: Xia cites Jungnickel–Vedder (1984), Thm 3.5, where TZ cite Feit.
findings.quote: Moreover, we derive from [8, Theorem 3.5] that n ≡ 0 (mod 8). Hence n ≡ 8 (mod 24).
findings.source: Xia v7 §4; ref [8] Jungnickel–Vedder, Europ. J. Combin. 5 (1984) 143–148
findings.stance: premise ledger should cite both sources
findings.specific_read_scope: proof of Thm 1.3 and reference list

findings.claim: Xia's systems are verified only at n=32, and the Gröbner computation fails at m=38. n=32 is already trivial for planes: 32²+32+1 = 1057 = 7·151.
findings.quote: The systems (11) and (12) are verified to have no solution when n = 32.

findings.claim: Xia's 2023 introduction cites Feit's 14400008 as the plane-order verification, not TZ's 2×10^11. No newer numerical bound is cited.
findings.quote: Conjecture 1.1 has been verified by Feit [4] for finite flag-transitive projective planes of order up to 14400008.

findings.claim: Xia's Math. Comp. paper excludes cyclotomic difference sets for even index m≤22 other than 2, 4, 8. For planes the index is n, so this covers only n≤22.
findings.quote: If m ≤ 22 is an even integer other than 2, 4 or 8, then neither H_{q,m} nor M_{q,m} forms a nontrivial difference set in F_q.

findings.claim: A 2018 survey still reports TZ as the state of the art. It conflates special pairs (classified only for p<10^7) with special primes (p<4×10^22).
findings.quote: Using nontrivial computations, Thas and Zagier [97] classified all special pairs (p,n), when p < 4 × 10^22; no surprises arise from the classification.

findings.claim: Baumert–Gordon exclude cyclic planes of non-prime-power order below 2×10^9. This covers a different and weaker range, and it does not cover prime-power n such as 2^(3^t).
findings.quote: no cyclic projective planes exist with non-prime power orders up to two billion.

findings.claim: OpenAlex lists 23 works citing TZ. The relevant ones are Xia 2017/2023, Xia 2018, the MWX survey, Gill 2016 and Boykett et al. 2025. No reported bound beyond 2×10^11 was found among them.
findings.quote: "cited_by_count": 23
findings.stance: search miss; not proof that no stronger bound exists

findings.claim: Author pages show no follow-up on flag-transitive planes after TZ. K. Thas lists only the 2003 survey and the 2008 paper. Zagier lists only #115. Xia lists EJC 2023 plus a 'challenge' on his characteristic-3 conjecture.
findings.quote: Prove or disprove: A conjeture on quadratic equations over finite fields of characteristic 3.
findings.date_or_version: fetched 2026-10-15; the Thas page looks unmaintained since about 2019

findings.claim: OEIS has no entry for the base-two exception sequence.
findings.quote: No results.

findings.claim: First step of WLW Prop 1 equals the lane's step 5 (the nonzero-support-XOR case).
findings.quote: By Lemma 2, W_f/4 mod 2 is affine. If it is constantly one, every magnitude is at most 20. If it is balanced, the mean square is at most (20^2 + 24^2)/2 = 488 < 512.
findings.stance: prior art two days before the lane's 15 Oct work

findings.claim: Second step of WLW Prop 1 equals the lane's steps 2–3. Together the two steps give: max|W|=24 forces |W|∈{8,24}, so W(0)≠0, so no balanced function has NL 244. This is elementary and does not use the Brier–Langevin part of the paper.
findings.quote: If q ≠ 1, Lemma 1 applied to 1 + q gives at least 128 zeros of q. On them |W_f| ≤ 16, so Σ W_f(a)^2 ≤ 128·16^2 + 384·24^2 = 253952 < 2^18.
findings.stance: prior art overlapping the lane's theorem A

findings.claim: WLW give a residue-degree lemma from the integer expansion W_f(a) = Σ_I (−2)^|I| a^I Σ_{x⊇I} (−1)^f(x). The same proof works for m=8 with r≤4.
findings.quote: In particular, for m = 9, if W_f ≡ c (mod 2^r) and 2 ≤ r ≤ 4, then deg((W_f − c)/2^r mod 2) ≤ r − 1.
findings.stance: the method underlying the lane's and the parent's residues

findings.claim: Canonical signed spectrum for odd-weight functions: multiply W by an affine sign to get W≡2 (mod 8); then (W−2)/8 mod 2 is quadratic, and a pointwise quadratic majorant is combined with Parseval. This is the parent's K/J construction, done for 9 variables.
findings.quote: Multiplication of W_f(a) by (−1)^ℓ(a) corresponds to an affine transformation of f, and normalizes the residue to W_f ≡ 2 (mod 8).
findings.stance: prior art for the parent's J_h and canonical-energy screen
findings.specific_read_scope: §5, proof of Thm 1, including 'q = (W_f − 2)/8 mod 2 is quadratic' and (32) W² ≤ 4W + 252 + 320q

findings.claim: Fixed-half capacity on two 8-variable restrictions of a 9-variable function, combined with Parseval.
findings.quote: Let A and B be the 8-variable Walsh transforms of its two restrictions. For each frequency, A + B, A − B ∈ {±8, ±24}, |A| + |B| ≤ 24.

findings.claim: Energy/ℓ¹ technique: a quadratic majorant of |z| on a residue class, combined with Walsh inversion and Parseval.
findings.quote: For integers z ≡ 1 (mod 4), define Φ(z) = (3z² − 2z + 15)/16. Then |z| ≤ Φ(z).
findings.stance: closest known analogue of the parent's canonical-energy ℓ¹ screen

findings.claim: Balanced 242 is still open as of 13 Oct 2026.
findings.quote: it is still an open problem to determine whether there exists a balanced 9-variable Boolean function with nonlinearity 242

findings.claim: Support-XOR congruence for balanced functions (8 variables; the derivation does not depend on n).
findings.quote: Therefore, W_f(ω) ≡ 4ω · b (mod 8). If b = 0, then W_f(ω) is a multiple of 8 and |W_f(ω)| ≤ 16.
findings.source: Lou–Xu–Wang §3, with b = XOR of supp(f)
findings.stance: prior art for the lane's s·a step

findings.claim: 2-adic quadratic residue for balanced 8-variable functions.
findings.quote: W_g(a,c) ≡ 4c + 8Q(a) (mod 16), for any (a,c) ∈ F_2^7 × F_2, where Q(a) ∈ B_7 is a quadratic function with Q(0) = 0.

findings.claim: Capacity bound on halves combined with Parseval, used in the 8-variable proof.
findings.quote: Since |2H₇v| = |W_g(a,1)| ≤ 20, we have |H₆v_L(a)| + |H₆v_R(a)| ≤ 10.
findings.stance: prior art for the capacity screen

findings.claim: The open-problem list repeats balanced 9-variable NL 242.
findings.quote: Open problem 1. Does there exist a 9-variable balanced Boolean function with nonlinearity 242?

findings.claim: Kavut–Yücel state that their NL-242 functions have no Walsh zero, so none can be balanced by a linear shift.
findings.quote: However, there is no zero value in the Walsh spectra of these functions; hence, none of them can be linearly transformed to 9-variable balanced functions with nonlinearity 242.
findings.stance: consistent with the lane; the lane's neighborhood exclusions go further
findings.specific_read_scope: entire PDF, including Table 1 (upper bound 244 for n=9), the truth tables and Table 3

findings.claim: Classical degree-dependent divisibility. With m=0, d≤7, n=9 it gives 8|W for balanced functions of degree ≤7.
findings.quote: Let f be any n-variable m-resilient function and let d be its algebraic degree. The values of the Walsh transform of f are divisible by 2^(m+2+⌊(n−m−2)/d⌋).
findings.source: Carlet, chapter 'Boolean Functions for Cryptography and Error Correcting Codes', Prop 32 (crediting Carlet 2001 and Carlet–Sarkar 2002)
findings.stance: classical prior art for the divisibility half of the lane's theorem B
findings.specific_read_scope: §2.1 Prop 1, §2.2 Prop 9 and relation (28), §4.1 nonlinearity text, §7.1–7.2

findings.claim: The converse direction is also classical: 8|W implies degree ≤ n−2.
findings.quote: Assume that its Walsh transform takes values divisible by 2^k ... Then f has algebraic degree at most n − k + 1.
findings.specific_read_scope: Prop 9 and the remarks on its converse

findings.claim: The NNF–Fourier relation underlying all 2-adic residue-degree arguments.
As of 2006 and 2022, the maximum balanced NL was unknown for n≥8, with 240 the best known balanced value for n=9.
findings.quote: The maximum possible nonlinearity for balanced Boolean functions is unknown for all n > 7.
findings.source: Carlet et al., GECCO 2022, Table 1 (Max NL for n=9: 240); also Carlet chapter (2006): 'unknown for any n ≥ 8'
findings.specific_read_scope: §2 and Table 1; results tables (GP min/avg NL 240 at n=9)

findings.claim: Lou and Wang reportedly found 9-variable functions with exactly one Walsh zero.
findings.quote: functions in 7, 8 and 9 variables having one Walsh zero have been found by Lou and Wang

math: Exact matched conditions. The lane and TZ use the same reduction: Kantor (CFSG) → TZ Prop 2.1/Thm 2.4 (D = μ_{n+1} planar) → 8|n (Feit per TZ; Jungnickel–Vedder Thm 3.5 per Xia) → n≡2 (mod 3) from n^(n+1)≡1 (Xia derives it via the First Multiplier Theorem) → base-two necessity 2^(n+1)≡1 (mod p). Both restrict to the class n≡8 (mod 24).

Lane versus TZ range. TZ claim n<2×10^11 from a 3-day 2006–07 computation with no certificate. The lane's exact Python replay reaches n<251,539,607,552 (×1.258). The two paired C runs reach n<2,582,236,504,064 (×12.91), and the single C run reaches n<10,341,223,092,224 (×51.7). Both C results are empirical only.

Xia (2017/2023) is orthogonal: necessary characteristic-3 polynomial systems, checked only at n=32, which is trivial since 1057 = 7·151. Xia's Math. Comp. paper reaches index ≤22, also trivial for planes. Baumert–Gordon (2003) cover only non-prime-power n<2×10^9, so they miss prime-power candidates such as 2^(3^t).

What a fully exact replay to 2,582,236,504,064 would add, if correct and gap-free: the conditional exclusion would rise from TZ's n<2×10^11 to n<2.58×10^12 (p<≈6.67×10^24). It would be the first machine-replayable certificate beyond TZ, and the largest exclusion I located. It is the same base-two and proper-factor sieve as in TZ's appendix, so it is not a new method. It would still depend on CFSG via Kantor and on TZ's unreplayed range [5×10^9, 2×10^11). It cannot settle all orders.

Cheaper certification step: an exact replay of TZ's own range [5×10^9, 2×10^11), about 8.1×10^9 class members, would remove the dependence on an uncertified 2006 computation. That range is roughly 1/12 the size of the extension.
info: Lane theorem A (balanced maximum ∈ {240,242}). This follows directly from WLW Prop 1: max|W|=24 forces |W|∈{8,24}, hence W(0)≠0. Both of its inequalities (488<512 and 253952<2^18) match the lane's. The lane's W/4 ≡ s·a step corresponds to the support-XOR congruence in LXW §3. The lower bound 240 is the trivial quadratic example.

Lane theorem B (balanced and deg≤7 ⇒ NL≤240). Carlet Prop 32 with m=0, d=7, n=9 gives 8|W. The q-step of WLW Prop 1 with q(0)=0 then finishes in two lines. No source I read states B explicitly. Hou (1996), 'covering radius of RM(1,9) in RM(4,9) is 240', has a different hypothesis (deg≤4, any weight) and was not read.

Lane theorem C (a balanced 242 function has degree exactly 8 and nonzero support XOR). This follows from Möbius inversion of degree-8 coefficients (Carlet Prop 1) together with B. It is textbook level.

Fixed-half capacity |G|+|H|≤28 with Parseval is the same device as WLW Lemma 4 (|A|+|B|≤24 on the two 8-variable restrictions) and LXW (12). The specific ℓ¹ inequality (3570 + …) was not located; this is a search miss.

Parent's J_h for odd-weight 8-variable h. Write K = ±χ_s·H, normalized so that K≡2 (mod 8); this is WLW's normalization, and the sign flip is an affine transformation. Writing K = 2+8t gives (K²−4)/32 = t+2t², so J_h = (K−2)/8 mod 2. That is WLW's q with m=8. Lemma 2 still holds for m=8, r≤4, because the sums over nonempty proper I are even and the full-set term is 2^8. Equivalently, J=1 exactly when |H| mod 16 ∈ {6,10}, i.e. when the Jacobi symbol (2/(H/2)) = −1. This derivation is my own hand algebra, not computation-checked. No explicit earlier statement of the squared form was located.

Parent's canonical-energy screen, |K0−K| ≤ (m0²−m²)/4 and dist(FWHT K0, {±256}) ≤ (Σm0² − 65536)/4, belongs to the same family as WLW (11)–(13), (15)–(16) and (32): Walsh inversion, a quadratic majorant on a residue class, and Parseval. The exact inequality was not located.

significance.math: Modest, conditional and computational. If certified, the result is a quantitative extension of TZ's 2008 bound with replayable evidence. It brings no structural insight and no reduction in the CFSG dependence. Heuristically, under a naive 1/n chance that 2 is an n-th power residue and a prime density of about 1/12, the expected number of base-two survivors in [2×10^11, 2.58×10^12) is about 10^-2 [INFERENCE; falsifier: a correct density computation differing by orders of magnitude]. A null result therefore adds little evidence beyond TZ's own 'highly unlikely'. The lane's fixed-filter lemma correctly shows that sieves like this cannot settle all orders.
significance.info: The global elementary bounds look correct and were independently re-derived. Their priority, however, belongs at least to the 13 Oct 2026 preprints (WLW Prop 1; LXW §3) and to classical Carlet/Sarkar–Maitra divisibility. The defensible value is an explicit balanced-case corollary statement, not a new theorem. The fixed-half exclusions (251 of 252 classes provisionally) would be restricted-class computational results over a 124-source corpus. They are not global, and the existence of a balanced 242 function remains open.

counterpoints: All novelty and priority conclusions rest on searches: OpenAlex, two web searches, arXiv version probes, OEIS and author pages. Google Scholar and MathSciNet were not used, so a miss is not proof.
WLW and LXW are unrefereed v1 preprints. WLW Prop 1, however, is short and elementary and predates the lane's work by two days.
The lane's proof is logically independent of WLW, which is a genuine independent confirmation, but it is still not new.
TZ's numerical baseline is a prose claim, and the lane imports it. The lane's C runs reproduce only TZ's census below 5×10^9.
The source for 8|n is inconsistent across papers: Feit 1990 per TZ, Jungnickel–Vedder 1984 Thm 3.5 per Xia. Neither primary was read.
The MWX survey wording ('special pairs … p < 4×10^22') overstates TZ. Special pairs were classified only for p<10^7.
Xia (2023) cites Feit's 14400008 rather than TZ's 2×10^11 for the plane conjecture. This is an omission in his paper, not evidence of a weaker state of the art.
open_questions: Do Hou (DCC 1996; IEEE TIT 43 (1997) 1025–1027), Carlet (SETA 2001) or Brier–Langevin already state the W/8-mod-2-quadratic plus RM(2,9) argument for the balanced 9-variable case before 2026? All were inaccessible.
Is there any unindexed computation beyond TZ's 2×10^11, for example in a thesis, a forum post or a code repository? None was located.
Is there an explicit prior statement that (W²−4)/32 mod 2 is quadratic for odd-weight functions, or of a canonical-spectrum distance-to-{±256} bound? Neither was located.
Validity and exact hypotheses of Jungnickel–Vedder Thm 3.5 and Feit's 8|n proof: TZ accept the latter while rejecting Feit's power-of-two claim. Neither primary was read.
unverified_or_dropped: Feit, PAMS 108 (1990): HTTP 403. Its claims are cited only through TZ and Xia.
Jungnickel–Vedder 1984; K. Thas, Discrete Math. 266 (2003); Kantor, J. Algebra 106 (1987): not read.
Gill, TAMS 2016 (point-transitive planes, insoluble groups): not read; context only.
Boykett et al., Graphs and Combinatorics 2025 (cites TZ): CrossRef has no abstract; not read.
Hou 1996 and 1997; Sarkar–Maitra, CRYPTO 2000; Carlet, SETA 2001; Carlet–Sarkar, FFA 2002: read only through Carlet's 2006 chapter.
Carlet's 2021 book: the univ-paris13 host failed DNS, so the 2006 chapter mirror was used instead.
Evans–Van Veen (N=24): known only through the MWX survey.
OpenAlex entry 'Local analysis of cyclotomic difference sets' (2017, no DOI): probably an earlier arXiv title of Xia's paper [INFERENCE]; unchecked.
The lane's power-of-two family factorizations were not compared against Cunningham tables (out of scope).
new_evidence_vs_prior: Prior math ledger: TZ was read only through a staged reader, and novelty was 'unknown, no literature search'. New: the TZ primary is verified (seven exceptions below 5×10^9, the 3-day computation, Feit's attribution, the 2×10^22 vs 4×10^22 typo). No later stronger bound was found through Xia v7/EJC 2023, Xia 2018, the MWX 2018 survey, OpenAlex citers, the three author pages or OEIS. There is a second attribution for 8|n (Jungnickel–Vedder).

Prior info ledger: 'no novelty asserted; the method may be classical; independent of the 2026 preprint'. New: the exact two-inequality argument is WLW Prop 1 (13 Oct 2026), the support-XOR congruence is LXW §3, the divisibility half of B is Carlet Prop 32, and fixed-half capacity is WLW Lemma 4 and LXW (12). Kavut–Yücel explicitly state that their 242 functions have no Walsh zero. As of 13 Oct 2026 both preprints list balanced 242 as open, and neither has a v2.

For the parent's newest screens: J_h equals WLW's canonical q with m=8, and the energy-ℓ¹ screen belongs to WLW's Φ/(32) majorant-plus-Parseval family. The new part is applying them to fixed-half completions with per-coordinate caps 28−|G|.
